title: A pull request is locked as resolved, but never actually closed or merged
author: esu-elegba
description: Reads the repository's own pull request list and flags a PR whose active_lock_reason reads 'resolved' -- GitHub's own record of a maintainer's explicit claim that the matter is settled -- while its state still reads 'open'. The PR-side twin of locked-resolved-issue-still-open (the sixty-fourth real recipe): a pull request's own JSON object carries the identical locked/active_lock_reason fields an issue's does, because a PR is an issue under GitHub's own numbering and locking machinery, and GitHub's Lock API works identically on both. Locking a PR's conversation and actually merging or closing the PR it belongs to are two independent GitHub actions; nothing on GitHub's side ever compares a lock reason to the state field it implicitly claims something about.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long updated_at has sat still while active_lock_reason reads 'resolved' and state reads 'open' -- not flat. GitHub's pull request object has no locked_at field, so updated_at (the closest real signal GitHub exposes, moving whenever the PR's own metadata changes, including a lock) is used the same way locked-resolved-issue-still-open already uses it in place of a missing locked_at. Under 24 hours since the last update scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- the same person who just locked it may simply not have merged or closed it yet). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal read directly off two fields GitHub's own API already returns (active_lock_reason, state). The 24h window matches locked-resolved-issue-still-open's and the rest of the *-still-open family's own bar. A PR locked for a reason other than 'resolved' (off-topic, spam, too heated), locked with no reason recorded at all, not locked, already merged, already closed without merging, or carrying the malformed combination locked=false with a non-null active_lock_reason, is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- none of those states makes the 'resolved but still open' claim this recipe checks. Unlike an issue, a PR's own state is not two-valued: unblocked-pr-still-open and duplicate-pr-still-open (this library's current PR-fixture convention) both already read a merged PR's state as 'merged' and a closed-without-merging PR's state as 'closed', two distinct terminal values rather than a single 'closed' plus a separate boolean -- this recipe excludes on state != 'open' precisely because that one check already covers both terminal values, whichever one a given PR reached.
